open_points.subject: A20 Python runtime digest
open_points.question: What exact Python runtime artifact is identified by the digest that the release records and compares?
options: The installed interpreter executable or runtime tree
A named Python distribution or archive file
The Python layer or component supplied by the base image
open_points.default_guess: Use the digest of the exact Python distribution artifact installed into the release, named independently of the base image.

witness.initial: A candidate release names Python 3.13.1 and records all packages and the base image correctly.
events: The release builder installs Python from a distribution archive.
The installer compares the recorded Python digest before starting Registry.
outcomes: One implementation hashes the Python distribution archive and accepts the release.
Another hashes the installed interpreter or runtime tree, obtains a different digest and refuses the same release.
witness.observer: The release operator sees the same release accepted by one compliant implementation and refused by another.

open_points.subject: A20 dependency digests
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm and textual representation count as the required digest for packages, Python and the base image?
options: Require SHA-256 with an algorithm-qualified lowercase hexadecimal representation
Accept any algorithm named in the digest value
Use each artifact ecosystem's native digest scheme, which may differ by dependency kind
open_points.default_guess: Require an algorithm-qualified SHA-256 digest unless an ecosystem-mandated stronger scheme applies.

witness.initial: Two release manifests identify the same package distribution file; one records a SHA-256 digest and the other a SHA-1 digest.
events: Each release process verifies its recorded digest against the file.
outcomes: An implementation treating any matching cryptographic digest as sufficient makes both releases.
An implementation requiring SHA-256 refuses the SHA-1 release.
witness.observer: The release author sees different release-admission outcomes for the same artifact.

open_points.subject: A20 exact versions
open_points.text: without an exact version or a digest
open_points.question: What makes the version of a package, Python runtime or base image exact rather than incomplete?
options: Only a fully specified ecosystem version such as Python 3.13.1 and a non-floating image tag is exact
Any literal version or tag is exact when accompanied by the required digest
Exactness is defined separately for packages, Python and images by their respective version grammars
open_points.default_guess: Define exactness separately by dependency kind and reject ranges, wildcards and floating tags even when a digest is also present.

witness.initial: A candidate release names Python as 3.13 and a base image as registry.example/registry:3.13, each with a fixed digest.
events: The release process evaluates Required test 2's exact-version requirement.
outcomes: One implementation accepts because the literal versions plus digests identify fixed artifacts.
Another refuses because 3.13 omits a patch version and the image tag is considered floating.
witness.observer: The release author sees incompatible admission results.

open_points.subject: A20 release identity
open_points.text: the same release installed again gives the same list
open_points.question: What identifies a release, and may an existing release identifier ever be rebound to different release contents?
options: A release is identified by an immutable release-version value that can never be rebound
A release is identified by the digest of its complete release artifact, so the same human-readable version may denote distinct releases
A release is identified by a version plus build identity, with only the complete pair required to be immutable
open_points.default_guess: Identify a release by an immutable digest of its complete release artifact and prohibit rebinding every published release identifier.

witness.initial: Release label 1.0 has been installed with dependency list A.
events: A builder publishes another artifact under label 1.0 with dependency list B.
The installer evaluates whether rule 3 and Required test 4 allow it.
outcomes: An implementation treating label 1.0 as the release refuses the changed dependencies.
An implementation treating the new artifact digest as a new release accepts it despite the unchanged label.
witness.observer: The operator sees dependencies change under the same visible release label in one implementation but not the other.

open_points.subject: A20 dependency universe
open_points.text: After an installation that succeeded, the dependencies the running instance has are exactly the release's list, by name, version and digest, nothing more.
open_points.question: Are system libraries and the store engine represented only by the base-image entry, or must every individually loadable component inside that image also appear as its own named dependency?
options: The enumerated entries are exhaustive: packages and Python are individual entries, while the base-image digest collectively fixes its system libraries and store engine
Every runtime-loadable library and engine is also an individual dependency with its own name, version and digest
The base image is collective by default, but selected security-sensitive components must also be listed individually
open_points.default_guess: Treat the base-image digest as the collective identity of its system libraries and store engine; list Python packages and Python separately as the text expressly requires.

witness.initial: A release list contains every Python package, Python itself and the base image; that image contains libssl and the store engine.
events: Installation succeeds and the release process evaluates Required test 3.
Registry starts using libssl and the store engine from the image.
outcomes: One implementation accepts because the base-image entry collectively fixes those constituents.
Another refuses because libssl and the store engine are running dependencies absent as individual name/version/digest entries.
witness.observer: The release operator sees the same installed runtime pass or fail the exact-list guarantee.

open_points.subject: A20 Required test 2
open_points.text: A release whose list misses a package the instance would import, or names a package, the Python version or the base image without an exact version or a digest, is not made.
open_points.question: Must Required test 2 also show refusal when the list entirely omits the Python runtime or entirely omits the base image?
options: Add distinct missing-Python and missing-base-image cases
State that the existing missing-item case is parameterized over every dependency kind named by rule 1
Test only missing packages and rely on the normative rule without required evidence for omitted Python or base-image entries
open_points.default_guess: Require separate missing-Python and missing-base-image cases, or explicitly parameterize the missing-entry case over every dependency kind.

witness.initial: The release process has tests for a missing package and for present but incomplete package, Python and base-image entries; it has no case where Python or the base image is absent.
events: The release-process checks are run for admission.
A reviewer evaluates whether rule 1's completeness guarantee was shown.
outcomes: One implementation reports the Required tests satisfied because the only stated missing-entry case concerns a package.
Another reports them unsatisfied until omission of Python and omission of the base image are each shown to prevent release creation.
witness.observer: The release reviewer sees different pass results for the same evidence suite.

open_points.subject: A20 release dependency metadata
open_points.text: A release names every dependency it runs with, at an exact version, with its digest: every Python package, direct or transitive, by the digest of its distribution file; the Python version; and the base image of VM Platform's Registry environment by its digest, which fixes the system libraries and the store's engine.
open_points.question: In what generated artifact and schema are the dependency names, versions and digests represented?
options: One signed release manifest containing every dependency kind
An ecosystem lockfile for Python plus separate Python-runtime and OCI-image metadata
An SBOM accompanied by immutable references for the runtime and base image
consequences: A single schema simplifies completeness validation but requires generation to define all dependency kinds itself.
Native artifacts reduce duplication but require a deterministic rule for combining them into one release list.
An SBOM gives broad inventory coverage but requires a precise profile identifying authoritative version and digest fields.
open_points.requirement: A release names every dependency it runs with, at an exact version, with its digest: every Python package, direct or transitive, by the digest of its distribution file; the Python version; and the base image of VM Platform's Registry environment by its digest, which fixes the system libraries and the store's engine.
open_points.default_guess: Generate one immutable release manifest from the Python lock data, the selected Python runtime artifact and the OCI image reference.

open_points.subject: A20 Required test 2 evidence mechanism
open_points.text: A release whose list misses a package the instance would import, or names a package, the Python version or the base image without an exact version or a digest, is not made.
open_points.question: What factory check demonstrates the required release-creation refusals?
options: Schema and policy checks with a negative fixture for every missing or incomplete field
End-to-end attempts to build malformed releases and assertions that no release artifact is emitted
Both static negative fixtures and an end-to-end release-build refusal test
consequences: Static checks are fast and exhaustive over fields but do not alone show that the real release path cannot bypass them.
End-to-end checks exercise the real boundary but are slower and can leave individual malformed cases untested.
Combining both gives stronger evidence at greater maintenance cost.
open_points.requirement: A release whose list misses a package the instance would import, or names a package, the Python version or the base image without an exact version or a digest, is not made.
open_points.default_guess: Use exhaustive static negative fixtures plus one end-to-end assertion that a rejected definition emits no release artifact.
